exposure: Women with type 1 or gestational diabetes
Indication for IOL (suspected fetal macrosomia vs. other)
Women with no prior vaginal delivery
Women who underwent IOL for suspected non-diabetic fetal macrosomia
Stage of labor at time of previous CS (first stage arrest, second stage arrest, failed induction)
IOL for suspected non-diabetic fetal macrosomia
cohort: 660 women with a prior CS for failed labor induction or labor dystocia undergoing TOLAC
finding: While TOLAC was successful in 72.9% of cases, maternal height < 160 cm, no prior vaginal delivery, diabetes, IOL for suspected fetal macrosomia, and birth weight ≥4500 g were identified as risk factors for recurrent failed induction or labor dystocia.
mod_finding: The study found that trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC) was a feasible option compared to scheduled repeat cesarean section.
